TEXT.English: Unlike regular Fort Commanders, Nesting Spiders are beast units instead. They have 1 extra poison strength, 2 extra perception, and can get regular, combat related promotions instead of command promotions. As they gain levels, the gain [LINK=PROMOTION_FORTSPIDER1]Fort Spider I[\LINK] and [LINK=PROMOTION_FORTSPIDER2]Fort Spider II[\LINK] at level 3 and 5 respectively. [NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET]With Fort Spider I, they can turn any fortification into a [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_INFESTED_FORTRESS]Infested Fortress[\LINK] and [LINK=SPELL_SPAWN_BABY_SPIDER]summon a temporary baby spider[\LINK]. [NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET]With Fort Spider II, summoned baby spiders start with an extra strength.

TEXT.English: A fort appointed with a Fort Commander exerts your culture on the tile, with the culture boundry increasing as the fort ages, allowing you to claim nearby territory or resources without building a city. This can be ideal for providing a strong defensive location to hold a chokepoint, or a safe space in an open area to retreat your units and heal. As for the Commander themselves:[NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] A Fort Commander is a Commander type unit, allowing it to command and provide buffs to their minions. [NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] They gain free exp up to 20, allowing them to take further command promotions to specialize in different unit types. [NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] They gain extra strength with technology. 1 strength from Warfare and Military Strategy, and 2 from Engineering. [NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] Their strength may allow them to hold against a small enemy attack, but make sure to provide units for them to command for any serious assault. [NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] They cost 1 extra maintenence. [NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] They always provide a small strength boost to melee, ranged, and defensive melee units under their command.
